Flag days beyond thresholds

Source: R/calc_threshold_day.R
calc_threshold_day.Rd

For every unit and day, flags whether the value lies above or below each threshold, and how far beyond it lies. Replaces find_extr_abs_day() of climatic4economist.

Usage

calc_threshold_day(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
calc_threshold_day(
  x,
  above = NULL,
  below = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  chunk = "auto",
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A wide table from extract_*(), or a long table from an earlier indicator step.

...

Further arguments of the methods; the table method takes none.

above, below

Thresholds: numbers, or a table of thresholds by unit.

unit

Unit of the thresholds; defaults to the data's.

id

Optional name of the unit identifier column.

label

Optional name shown in progress messages.

chunk

"auto" splits the work by unit when it would not fit in memory; a whole number forces that many units per chunk; FALSE never splits.

Value

A long c4e_tbl: the unit identifiers, date, value, earlier indicator columns, and the new flag and excess columns.

Details

Thresholds are read in the unit of the data, which comes from upstream (see read_climate() and convert_unit()). A unit that contradicts the data is refused, so 30 is never compared with Kelvin by mistake.

A threshold is either a number, the same for every unit, or a table keyed by unit (and optionally by month) with one column per threshold, e.g. a threshold per agro-ecological zone or the percentiles of calc_percentile().

Flag columns are named after the time step and the threshold: day_abv_30, day_blw_0.1 (hr_ for hourly data, mo_ for monthly). Excess columns are named after the unit: C_abv_30, mm_blw_0.1. Each is described in the table's registry, which later steps read.

See also

calc_percentile_day(), calc_spell(), calc_condition()

Other indicators: calc_condition(), calc_heatwave(), calc_par(), calc_percentile(), calc_percentile_day(), calc_spell(), calc_spell_excess(), calc_spell_percentile(), calc_std_index(), calc_std_threshold()

Examples

tmax <- read_climate(
  system.file("extdata", "tmax_daily.tif", package = "c4e"))
#> Read tmax_daily: tmax [K], daily, 2021-01-01 to 2023-12-31, 1095 layers
#> (synthetic).
survey <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
coord <- prepare_coord(survey, lat_var = lat, lon_var = lon)
points <- georef_coord(coord, geom = c("lon", "lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326")

extract_by_coord(tmax[[1:60]], points) |>
  convert_unit("C") |>
  calc_threshold_day(above = c(30, 35))
